title: Phonological Short Term Memory tasks for Italian-English comparison
author: Chiara Valeria Marinelli
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.96nh9de

steps.title: Conduct Non-Word Repetition Task
steps.instruction: Measure phonological short-term memory using bi-syllabic non-words read aloud to the subject.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the child: “I am going to say some invented words. Please listen carefully and repeat them immediately after me, in the same order.”
Read ten lists of three bi-syllabic (5 letters) non-words at a pace of approximately one word every 2 seconds.
Ask the child to repeat each list as accurately as possible immediately after the experimenter finishes speaking.
Score the task by awarding one point for each correct non-word, for a maximum score of 30.

steps.title: Conduct Digit Span Task
steps.instruction: Measure phonological short-term memory by asking the subject to repeat lists of digits of increasing length.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the child: “I am going to say some numbers. Please listen carefully and repeat them immediately after me, in the same order.”
Begin with lists of length L=4, reading numbers with an interval of approximately 1 to 2 seconds between them.
If the subject makes mistakes with L=4, present lists of length L=3.
Progress to longer lists (L=5, L=6, etc.), presenting ten lists for each length.
Terminate the task when the subject cannot recall more than two lists of a given length.

steps.title: Score Digit Span Task
steps.instruction: Calculate the total span score based on the number of sequences recalled correctly.

substeps.instruction: Assign 0.1 point for each sequence recalled correctly (10 correct sequences = 1 point).
If all ten sequences for L=4 are recalled correctly, start the base score at 4.0.
If L=3 was required, assume performance for lengths 2 and 3 is completely correct.
Sum the scores obtained for each length to determine the final span.
